Elon Musk's xAI data centers in Memphis and Southaven are accused of poisoning residents by operating dozens of methane gas turbines without full Clean Air Act permits, releasing toxic pollutants like nitrogen oxides (NOx) and formaldehyde into historically Black neighborhoods.  The facilities, powering the "Colossus" supercomputers, have become a focal point for allegations of environmental racism, as they operate in communities already burdened by high cancer risks and asthma rates. 

Unpermitted Operations and Emissions. Reports indicate xAI installed up to 35 portable gas turbines in Memphis and 27 in Southaven, Mississippi, bypassing standard permitting processes by classifying them as temporary generators.  These turbines emit an estimated 1,200 to 2,000 tons of nitrogen oxides annually in Memphis alone, surpassing emissions from nearby industrial plants, while lacking the pollution controls typically required by federal law.  Residents in areas like Boxtown report worsening respiratory conditions, with advocates describing the situation as a public health crisis driven by unregulated industrial expansion. 

Legal Action and Community Response. The NAACP, represented by the Southern Environmental Law Center and Earthjustice, has filed lawsuits alleging violations of the Clean Air Act and seeking to halt operations until proper controls are installed.  Community leaders and state representatives have labeled these neighborhoods "sacrifice zones," noting that African Americans are 75% more likely to live near toxic facilities.  While xAI has secured some permits retroactively, critics argue the rapid construction—completed in just 122 days for the first facility—was designed to evade public scrutiny and regulatory oversight.
